cycles.title: The Older Inhabited World
cycles.eyebrow: Kingdoms, commercial roads and metropolitan inheritances occupy an already old world.
cycles.description: Water settlements, territorial crowns and trading towns share a landscape of paid work and older structures. Colleges send skilled people along the same roads used by armies, care workers and merchants. Later metropolitan societies retain worked objects and living crossings; Nell and Bash inhabit a low-magic trough after earlier technological and magical ages.
cycles.sequenceNote: This proposed orbit contains several overlapping regional histories and a later modern reach. The transition to Nell’s trough orders the reconstruction without assigning one common collapse to its earlier societies. Windows are schematic placements, not conversions of local years into orbital duration.

eras.title: The inland watersheds and marches
eras.description: Cultivated watersheds, service compacts and military roads sustain neighboring settlements and expanding crowns.
context: Harvest crews, mills, cisterns and trained healers support settled populations.
Lock tolls, powder, crossbows, forage and engineering give territorial claims their practical reach.
eras.sequenceNote: The Eagle Queen’s century of succession and the held sunset’s twenty outside years remain local histories. Settlements and campaigns overlap; their institutions do not begin together.

eras.title: The chartered towns
eras.description: Court patronage, hereditary houses and ordinary paid livelihoods meet in commercially mature towns.
context: Tax, rent, household service and credit connect powerful patrons to working shops.
Coaches, smoking trams, care work, theaters, restaurants and apprenticeships support lives beyond the court.
eras.sequenceNote: Mundane civic lives belong in this magic-active world without requiring a magical explanation. The towns are proposed regional neighbors with different rulers, institutions and local clocks.

eras.title: The colleges and the signal roads
eras.description: Qualified work and distributed signals connect cities to rural districts, sanctuary polities and older roadside structures.
context: Teaching, assessment, road rotations and repair contracts carry expertise between settlements.
Optical relays and civic service bargains remain useful when a central court fails; a bookmender encounters an imperial-age tower.
eras.sequenceNote: Kethra’s qualification precedes her apprenticeship story. Other colleges, signal polities and trades share a proposed historical reach; the Cinder Annex retains an unresolved physical coordinate.

eras.title: The caravan and expedition corridors
eras.description: Caravan settlements, mines and expedition towns turn difficult landscapes and inherited structures into livelihoods.
context: Cooling contracts, freight credit, mine work and dockside processing keep trade moving.
Paid delvers and relic hunters encounter structures that were already old before their expeditions.
eras.sequenceNote: Resource work overlaps with the chartered towns and colleges. The Night Harvest’s underlying category and old-versus-new position remain unresolved; this is its proposed operating context.

eras.title: The metropolitan inheritances
eras.description: Modern transport, property services and household routines coexist with worked objects, private faculties and older crossing customs.
context: Certified doorway work, courier apps, municipal road crews and clinics make an inhabited modern service world.
Objects and practices can outlast their first owners while their meanings become incomplete or contested.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed overlapping metropolitan communities. Ryo’s destinations, Deepmarket and dream encounters retain their own unresolved coordinates; their material frames remain before extinction.

eras.title: Nell and Bash’s low-magic home
eras.description: One familiar modern society treats magic largely as a story after earlier ages of technology and active power.
context: Philadelphia and Cambridge continue their ordinary routines around two brief departures.
Nell and Bash bring 617 shared days in Ravel back into separate home clocks.
eras.sequenceNote: This home era precedes later divine rises and the Glass Sea. Ravel is another pre-extinction era of the same world, with its order relative to those eras unresolved.

cycles.title: The Returning Sovereignties
cycles.eyebrow: Gods, human governments and a public magical sky follow different fortunes.
cycles.description: After Nell’s older modernity, later states again govern through living gods, inherited offices and extraordinary public capacities. Human courts and commercial ports operate beside them. Some governments give up divine or dynastic claims while other institutions continue; the magical-girl circles decline on their own clock. Far later, the Glass Sea repairs a different political and physical inheritance.
cycles.sequenceNote: Divine resurgence follows Nell’s home in this reconstruction. The Bay arc and the Glass Sea provide ordered landmarks within a plural world; local abdications, forest succession and regional disasters are not one shared fall.

eras.title: The watershed states and harbor jurisdictions
eras.description: Long-lived rulers, human dynasties and commercial jurisdictions negotiate authority over water, roads, households and promised futures.
context: Dragon labor, divine adjudication, forecasts and ordinary courts support distinct states.
Abdication, a restored capital and a vacant throne change governments while ports, granaries and household lives continue.
eras.sequenceNote: The two dragon administrations are a proposed historical family of rival solutions, not one polity. Each succession and institutional change retains its own local interval.

eras.title: The inhabited public sky
eras.description: Schools, modern households and municipal economies accommodate powers with very different degrees of public recognition.
context: Laboratory work, clinics, delivery flight and agricultural weather coexist with ordinary phones and transport.
Northbridge’s distributed help and Brackenport’s exclusion of hero economies are different local responses to public power; Cusco retains its own divine household.
eras.sequenceNote: Attendance leads directly to Help. Help and Not About That precede the Bay in the supplied sequence; no common school, city or descent of Solstice’s circles is established.

eras.title: The forests and occupied foundations
eras.description: Forests, refuges and long-inhabited ground change around people whose memories outlast particular kingdoms.
context: Royal land becomes pasture, orchard and woodland while a living forest system persists.
Old mortuary structures shelter refugees; another settlement must move when its supposedly permanent ground stirs.
eras.sequenceNote: These local landscape histories overlap the functioning states. The moving colossus establishes neither divine resurrection nor a common cause for other catastrophes.

eras.title: The Bay and its long aftermath
eras.description: The last magical girl defends an evacuated bay after her circles have already vanished; later institutions inherit the event unevenly.
context: Solstice’s coronation precedes the battle by centuries.
Damaged recovery records and a museum centuries later produce different errors about who survived and what happened.
eras.sequenceNote: Battle, detention aftermath and museum stay in order within one local trajectory. The museum’s pre-extinction placement is editorial; its witness is Solstice, not the prisoner.

eras.title: The Glass Sea and the working border cities
eras.description: Living powers and technical crews sustain cities over the physical remains of earlier political decisions.
context: The Glass Sea preserves four centuries of centralized solar dependence after the Day of Glass.
Vantress combines living powers, ceramic structures and pressure signals in a different civic network.
eras.sequenceNote: The Glass Sea follows Nell and the Bay. Its second dawn is a specific recovery; Vantress supplies a compatible municipal context without sharing that catastrophe or solar root.

cycles.title: The Extinction and the Human Works
cycles.eyebrow: A vigorous magical world ends; later people build and lose wonders of their own.
cycles.description: The Ascendancy grows from armistice councils after route wars and furnace invasions, seeking to bind every root while magical cities and societies remain active. All Accounts Due ends that material capacity. After an unmeasured interval, secular engineering cultures keep cities, workshops and maritime communities working. Orison’s permanent grounding is one later technical loss; other inhabited places continue.
cycles.sequenceNote: Extinction lies inside this proposed orbit. Every subsequent reach is perfectly magicless; matter, populations and ordinary knowledge can persist. The schematic gap after extinction represents an unmeasured history, not an immediate reconstruction generation.

eras.title: The Ascendancy and the last accounting
eras.description: A postwar institution turns a vigorous, connected magical world toward universal compulsion and an irreversible response.
context: The Array is already 302 years old; Faris’s thirty-one years of travel encounter active cities, palaces and distinct living systems.
All six terminal conditions end the old roots and their restoration paths.
eras.sequenceNote: This is the universal extinction boundary, not the aftermath of the Bay or the Day of Glass. The later reaches of this orbit retain no old magical capacity.

eras.title: The working machine cities
eras.description: Material cities sustain practical expertise through paid workshops, maintenance and repeated repair.
context: Coal, steam, quarry work and speaking-wire signals organize civic labor.
A century of alloy repair and a failing municipal machine expose how technical knowledge is kept through work.
eras.sequenceNote: These are operating industrial traditions within the Long Dark. Their cities and dates are distinct; neither is a first generation after extinction.

eras.title: The inhabited machine coasts
eras.description: Engineered mobile communities depend on maintained structures, weather knowledge and populations capable of living through failure.
context: A sailing commonwealth keeps hulls, gardens, forges and mechanical forecasts in service.
Orison’s nuclear lift system fails irreversibly; surviving residents must leave by sea.
eras.sequenceNote: The maritime settings share a proposed technical reach, not a fleet or sea. Orison remembers human building after magic’s death; its grounding leaves other communities and technologies intact.

eras.title: The arsenal beyond remembered knowledge
eras.description: A later agrarian community encounters technical capacity whose purpose it can no longer identify.
context: The launch facility survives physically while its operating knowledge is inaccessible.
The finders leave its controls unused and mark the hazardous route for others.
eras.sequenceNote: Placing this knowledge loss after a represented nuclear height is a historical proposal. The facility is not Orison, and neither its builders’ fate nor an earlier launch is established.

cycles.title: The Human Refoundings
cycles.eyebrow: Ordinary modernity, reconstructed antiquity and another technological height.
cycles.description: Ordinary modern life occupies one island of the Long Dark. Later institutions reconstruct bodies and ancient identities, while Merneith builds a new empire through water and energy infrastructure. Other cities administer living buildings, modified bodies and recorded identities. Planetary engineering, military foundries and civilian orbital trades coexist in this reach rather than forming separate steps toward space.
cycles.sequenceNote: Modernity and the Queen’s reconstruction share one proposed orbital interval; the story’s ten-thousand-year antiquity and sixty-year rise remain local spans. The later technical contexts overlap without one common invention, dynasty or universal level of access.

eras.title: The ordinary modern island
eras.description: Ordinary work, care, relationships and captured civic power occupy a familiar modern world with unequal neighbors.
context: Cafes, festivals, arts venues, schools, transport and medicine sustain ordinary lives.
The closed-border journey encounters an industrial orc society at the same time as its isolated agrarian neighbor.
eras.sequenceNote: Our ordinary modern time belongs to the Long Dark. Ruth is placed by her originating life; the afterlife station remains outside the material clock. No literal Seattle history is automatically imported.

eras.title: The inhabited technical cities
eras.description: Technical capacity reaches apartments, clinics, public buildings and the institutions that control movement and identity.
context: Home workshops and aftermarket repair coexist with living housing, routine body plans and broadcast arenas.
Older masonry, freight margins and eleven simultaneous building traditions remain part of working cities.
eras.sequenceNote: These cities form a proposed broad technical horizon with unequal services and different histories. Architectural variety and inhabited manual margins do not imply a single intervening collapse.

eras.title: The planetary infrastructure states
eras.description: States extend their authority through continental utilities and orbital engineering.
context: Reconstructed ancient identities become a new political project rather than restored ancient minds.
Water, energy, weather satellites and defended ground stations give public authority material reach.
eras.sequenceNote: Merneith’s sixty-year rise is explicit; her ancient sources have their own dates. The other orbital-defense state is a contextual neighbor, not an identified successor government.

eras.title: The ground and orbital working world
eras.description: Military and civilian institutions use bodies, neural systems and maintained orbital structures in the same broad technical reach.
context: Civilian repair lives remain entangled with military overrides and an abandoned orbital foundry.
Paid tug crews, refinery cargo and inhabited defense stations still require bounded experiments and practical maintenance.
eras.sequenceNote: The military and civilian histories overlap by proposal. Their technologies and commands are distinct; an abandoned foundry does not mean all orbital civilization has ended.

cycles.title: The Divided World and the Joined Sky
cycles.eyebrow: Road cultures and working orbits diverge; the oldest fast roads close before new magic begins.
cycles.description: Some surface communities live by caravan work, salvage and inherited bodily adaptations while technically capable societies remain overhead. Ground and orbit misremember one another. The First People’s ancient stellar network finally burns, leaving inhabited worlds and slower aid routes. Much later, the first reciprocal link appears over the already inhabited world and ends the perfect material zero.
cycles.sequenceNote: Different losses of knowledge coexist with maintained technology. The stellar root burn and reawakening are distinct events, separated here by an unmeasured interval; new magic does not restore either old magical systems or the destroyed stellar network.

eras.title: The inhabited road and water worlds
eras.description: Road communities, occupied underground spaces and contested watersheds sustain lives among uneven inheritances.
context: A civic engine survives in a salvage economy; freight adaptations persist in a population after their original methods become disputed.
Ordinary organism behavior, route knowledge, rifles and obsolete sensors support different communities.
eras.sequenceNote: These societies need not share one collapse or ancestor. Some technical loss is explicit, while other apparent ruins are inhabited places misread by outsiders.

eras.title: The inhabited ground and working sky
eras.description: Surface and orbital populations continue simultaneously while their maps, histories and uses of old structures diverge.
context: A false account of surface abandonment and obsolete descent maps obscure living communities below.
An ancient sunshade remains entangled with ground power grids, tug work and a new ordinary ecology.
eras.sequenceNote: The ground–orbit contrasts are explicit within each story. They are proposed neighbors here, not a universal evolutionary sequence or one abandoned station network.

eras.title: The last fast roads and the slower sky
eras.description: An inherited interstellar network ends while living communities and advanced vessels remain.
context: Humanity’s oldest roads predate the younger stellar civilizations that later use them.
After the root burn, slower rescue remains possible; a later proposed stranded vessel recovers only a local orbital route.
eras.sequenceNote: The First People’s root burn is explicit. The stranded traveler follows it by proposal; the burn does not explain that vessel’s memory damage or identify its technology.

eras.title: The first answer across the joined sky
eras.description: Two living answers across an external boundary begin a new material working in an already inhabited world.
context: Ordinary light carries the extinct world’s final image through ages of perfect zero without carrying a mind or magical seed.
The first bilateral link changes both participants’ worlds; other living pairs attempt their own replies.
eras.sequenceNote: This is the reawakening boundary. Earlier scenes in the same story belong to extinction and the Long Dark; the first link restores none of the six old systems.

cycles.title: The New Inhabited World
cycles.eyebrow: New magic enters many kinds of society, and local failures leave the wider world alive.
cycles.description: After an unmeasured interval, mature new-magical communities include agricultural kingdoms, modern towns, public heroes and private kin groups. Cities depend on ordinary services as well as extraordinary inhabitants; older local agreements accumulate their own histories. The Salt Crucible supplies one proposed later regional catastrophe, with millions elsewhere continuing ordinary life.
cycles.sequenceNote: These are mature societies rather than the first generation after reawakening. Their different institutions and powers can overlap regionally. The Crucible’s new-era position is proposed; its local fire is neither a universal extinction nor a restoration of old roots.

eras.title: The working settlements and water kingdoms
eras.description: Settled communities and mobile polities negotiate the land, routes and water that support their livelihoods.
context: Sheepfolds, halls, mills, irrigation and ordinary craft continue around distinct living workings.
An orchard kingdom and a mobile cloud city occupy different positions in the same water system.
eras.sequenceNote: The cloud and land societies are simultaneous within their story. The Players Above is placed by its material town; the external players’ coordinates remain open.

eras.title: The modern towns and their older obligations
eras.description: Modern towns contain long local obligations, ordinary employment and households that have learned different ways to live with their inhabitants.
context: Flood works, property services, local worship, clinics and transport provide a shared material setting.
Old promises, divine debts, bodily practices and household accommodations retain their own histories and limits.
eras.sequenceNote: Public services and private knowledge can coexist. Evadne’s 114-year photograph and the grandmother’s forty-six-year interval are local spans, not the founding dates of a universal new culture.

eras.title: The public cities and their connected margins
eras.description: Civic institutions accommodate extraordinary bodies, professional heroes and travelers whose experiences do not fit one local clock.
context: Hospitals, schools, utilities, legal hearings and technical equipment make public capacities part of ordinary work.
A human college’s contact with an external court coexists with local bodily conventions and unexplained journeys.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed metropolitan and regional neighbors, not one agency or population-wide power system. External destinations retain their own coordinates; court and college are simultaneous.

eras.title: The Salt Crucible and the surviving countryside
eras.description: A premature release of worldfire destroys one region while the wider inhabited world survives.
context: An earlier rural household and ordinary travel precede the pair’s journey to the Crucible.
A valley and the western basin edge burn; surviving fields, roofs and millions of ordinary lives remain beyond them.
eras.sequenceNote: The final prose supplies the local extent of the catastrophe. Its placement after reawakening is an editorial proposal; no shared fire root, following collapse or origin of later societies is asserted.

cycles.title: The Later Refoundings
cycles.eyebrow: Working craft, long memories and advanced excavations share a later inhabited world.
cycles.description: Later societies keep tram-served clinics, workshop trades and living public works in operation while older institutions acquire new uses or fall into neglect. Practitioners encounter personal memories and cult claims far older than their current professions. Elsewhere, technically sophisticated excavators reinterpret inherited landscapes and meet a village displaced by millions of years. Craft and advanced archaeology coexist; neither defines the final form of civilization.
cycles.sequenceNote: This is a proposed later reach with independent institutional histories. The Salt Crucible does not found these societies. Kettlebridge’s arrival shares an archaeological horizon with the coastal expedition without being declared the latest event or identifying their peoples, sites or tools.

eras.title: The tram and workshop societies
eras.description: Industrial societies maintain specialized body care, memory work and communication systems with histories of their own.
context: Trams, clinical records, workrooms, ultraviolet lamps, valves and broadcasts support distinct professions and populations.
A client who estimates his age at twenty-five thousand years recalls an undated early battle; an abandoned cult sanctuary provides a different encounter with older lives.
eras.sequenceNote: The remembered battle, later refuge and factory scenes are personal spans rather than entire Galactic Cycles. Birth-channel rules and the predictive eye remain distinct local systems.

eras.title: The civic engines and inhabited older buildings
eras.description: Municipal labor, salvage and restoration keep cities inhabited as buildings and artifacts change hands and purposes.
context: Spellwrights, winchwrights, ward crews and a bounded death god sustain public works.
Estate collections and a hall rebuilt across generations expose maintenance obligations and coerced living labor.
eras.sequenceNote: The hall’s decline and smaller reopening are one actual local refounding. Other cities share a proposed craft horizon without becoming descendants of its colony or builders.

eras.title: The excavated shores and returning village
eras.description: Archaeological institutions confront physical landscapes that do not support their simple stories of royal origins.
context: A coastal expedition finds repeated communal repairs and possible deliberate retreat beneath a drowned-king tradition.
A mechanized excavation receives an intact village on the bedrock from which it vanished millions of years earlier.
eras.sequenceNote: Their shared late horizon is proposed, not a common institution or measured ordering. Kettlebridge’s departure and crossing mechanism remain unresolved; the upward water remains unclassified.

where-the-white-elk-went.note: More than three thousand autumns turn royal halls into fields, orchards and woods around one enduring witness. Its present is an inhabited palimpsest with a specific long local history.

the-last-flames.note: A long-lived keeper’s mortuary practice outlasts kingdoms she can still place. She adapts its apparatus to shelter living refugees after an elder’s death. The structures’ age and the northern catastrophe’s wider reach remain unknown.

the-villages-only-mage.note: A mountain village's mill, cistern and road depend on many accumulated living favors. Visiting certified surveyors connect that rural network to a wider professional culture; the village is not simply an earlier stage than the city.

the-ninety-year-barrier.note: A village's mills, craft work and safety depend on ninety years of a living witch's maintenance. It belongs with established watershed services, not an age before civic organization.

every-flower-she-knew.note: Eleven seasons of professional plant work connect healer, millwright and channel crews. Seasonal water logistics and trained observation place this settlement within a working rural service economy.

blood-types-of-immortality.note: Nine years of blood research take place beside mill work, winter travel and ordinary healing. The failed coercive experiment belongs to this rural technical culture; it does not establish successful immortality.

tea-for-the-first-guest.note: A roughly two-thousand-year-old tower recalls imperial leaf duties, grain fleets and horse relays while its present visitor repairs account books in a printing, coach and paid-lodging economy. The present belongs with commercial roads; the older political world is an internal historical span.

the-unfinished-sunset.note: Arveth refuses a grain seizure, then traps her own village while trying to divert the pursuing patrol. Twenty outside years and remembered repetitions of forty-three minutes expose the cost of her choice inside a collective agricultural working.

the-lions-last-constellation.note: A council, trained champion and witnesses confront a failing spring system. Bounded constellation work supplements an organized agrarian polity rather than founding one.

never-a-mascot.note: Royal armor work and seven years of campaigning put extraordinary animal capacity inside a territorial war economy. The bird's resistance interrupts military appropriation; it does not end war everywhere.

when-the-eagle-bowed.note: A living armor colony carries memory from the executed Eagle Queen through a century of successor crowns. Toll roads and upland livelihoods place that actual succession beside other territorial compacts.

the-gentlest-terror.note: Dragon watch, rescue and nesting rights already form an old service compact. A succession crisis tests mature institutions; the king's death is recent, while the founding obligation is much older.

strength-of-ten.note: An established old-magical history of lock tolls, grain depots and military roads. Sigrun's command is capped at twenty days; the compact assigns one-third of lock tolls to wages, injured households, roads and displaced villages for seven years.

the-bride-who-came-back.note: Three dynasties have turned annual bridal sacrifice into a glass-and-heat system for furnaces, baths and streets. The twenty-three-day crisis belongs to an urban resource state, not merely an early marriage custom.

the-vacant-throne.note: Fifteen years of vacancy after a border war end in witnessed accession. The demon queen’s signet once administered granaries, marriages and troop roads. Political evidence and ongoing civic work fit the later old governments without a magical succession rule.

mother-of-monsters.note: A powder-using army attacks a mixed refuge built around old gates and culverts. Military engineering, displaced communities and a living defensive curse make this a contested frontier rather than a mythic origin of monsters.

the-kingdom-of-later.note: A rented cobbler's shop, taxation and delayed royal reimbursements expose the gap between court favor and a town's cash economy. Its living postponement working operates inside established trade and law.

the-shape-of-mercy.note: An aristocratic household rules tenants and orchards while a child conceals a desire-gift for ten years. Patronage, inheritance and ordinary records locate this history beside other households shaped by chartered authority.

the-sister-behind-her-smile.note: Palace seamstresses, paid grace work and acoustic craft make appearance a professional service. Six days of suppression lead to a review two years later; this is a labor and patronage history within a wealthy court.

a-note-of-spite.note: Perfume, anti-hex commodities, hired servants and drawing-room committees support a mature consumer enchantment economy. A thirty-year friendship gives the birthday crisis its local depth.

the-second-wearing.note: A sentient pendant survives thirty-one boxed years, several moves and family performances before entering a modern household. Wearable craft, inherited objects and ordinary work give it close contextual neighbors in this older modernity.

the-last-thing-i-could-fix.note: A valley repair shop services unlike magical devices for a court-appointed hero. Reservoir damage and an overloaded armor circuit tie specialist craft to public infrastructure and the terms of paid work.

where-it-hurts.note: Hiring fairs, expedition lists, souvenirs and winter lodging sustain professional adventurers. A living blade's emotional cost breaks a four-year partnership inside that commercial network.

the-seventh-night.note: A contracted delver's seven-day bodily crisis unfolds amid inns, hired travel and printed scandal. Its commercial expedition culture closely fits Where It Hurts; no shared expedition or curse is established.

clerics-infernal-ex.note: A twenty-year shelter circuit and a bounded traveling appointment connect religious care to carters, roads and labor obligations. The kiln court and living portal have their own unresolved external coordinates.

fourth-house.note: Municipal assessors, guilds, insurance and permits regulate a clay worker's craft. Ten years of Gifted practice and a ten-day case for Cultivated work belong to an established urban service economy.

voice-of-silence.note: Four years of research and an examination rescue change Kethra's standing within a callwright college. Its living geometry and hand language form the established first half of the Kethra pair.

a-lock-on-the-inside.note: Kethra is now archmage during a seven-day apprentice trial. This follows Voice of Silence in the same teaching institution; the interval between the stories remains unspecified.

the-weight-of-falling-up-rune-shoes.note: A collegium teaches practical flight through roof surveys while brooms, winged horses and rune shoes coexist. That institutional training belongs to the circulation of technical skills, not a single universal flight technology.

the-healers-measure.note: Fees, sponsorship, service terms and a twenty-seven-month capstone lead into road rotations and recurring training. Formal education feeds an itinerant public-health profession.

the-thousandth-fall.note: A season of private self-mending practice culminates in a pilgrim-bridge rescue. Grain traffic, couriers and a cloister place it among road services; the story establishes no licensing examination.

the-friends-i-built.note: The Cinder Annex supports schools, dispatch, transport and technical exhibitions. Its educational economy fits this horizon, but neither its material-world location nor its relation to other infernal realms is established.

the-door-knows-home.note: Locksmith certification, estate law, appraisers and electrically served streets support a public doorway trade. Thousands of a mother's uses have made a specific dwelling recognizable; familiarity is not transferable property ownership.

an-ordinary-education.note: A laboratory-created magicless student enters a modern society of public powers, school selection, phones and transport. Its mature scientific and magical institutions support the proposed later public-power reach; they are not dated by Nell’s trough.

not-about-that.note: Delivery work, municipal weather, roof schooling and family practice make public flight ordinary city life. Its supplied reading position is before the Bay; no shared city or direct lineage to Solstice is established.

the-small-moon-rose-first.note: Nell and Bash return to Philadelphia and Cambridge after 617 shared days in Ravel, only seconds after their separate departures. Their low-magic home precedes later divine rises and the Glass Sea. Ravel is another pre-extinction era of this same physical world, with no established order relative to their home.

a-knock-in-someone-elses-sleep.note: A quarry becomes holiday cottages while the same living mineral contact reaches two childhoods separated by sixty years. Roads, coach travel and locally concealed experience place the present within a modernity with older material layers.

a-crown-of-quiet-hours.note: A 218-year pacification order depends on dragon labor, hydraulic administration and worship of fabricated dead rulers. Its political redesign belongs beside long-lived governments; that worship never establishes actual godhood.

the-peace-they-could-sleep-through.note: Two centuries of roads, grain and collective divine adjudication create a government that cannot keep delegating every judgment upward. Its institutional transition parallels the other long reign without sharing its dragons or false masks.

fifty-seven-minutes.note: A commercial harbor's insurance, registers and court procedures meet eighty-six years of agelessness and fifty-seven minutes of actual godhood. Authority is local to this maritime crisis, not a universal new pantheon.

head-priests-in-love.note: Two priests in their seventh year of cooperation perform a Brackwater rite that has survived 112 circuits. Departure and mooring rites already serve a commercial port under distinct gods and covenants.

saint-and-demon.note: Travel, an eight-month rural household and the Salt Crucible precede a catastrophe confined to a valley and the western basin edge while millions elsewhere survive. This is a proposed post-reawakening placement for a local magical loss; the final prose establishes no shared old root or universal extinction.

a-little-winter-for-sale.note: A desert settlement's stills, freight credit and wages depend on bounded, paid dragon cooling. The heat service and its maintenance contract connect this caravan economy to other specialist public works without identifying their makers.

the-night-harvest.note: A three-month ecological arrival becomes a dockside industry of hides, fuel, clinic material and debt. Six nights expose a local node's effects; the phenomenon's category and old-versus-new placement remain unresolved.

a-crown-for-the-endless-fire.note: Paid mine workers maintain vents and recently serviced stairs above older relief works. This is an operating extraction economy layered over inherited engineering, not proof that the surrounding civilization has collapsed.

the-name-the-water-took.note: A paid inland survey threatens settlements whose agronomy the captain wants to claim. Maps, guide coercion and a bounded amnesia pool place this encounter on an expanding resource frontier.

stay-out-of-my-city.note: Nine years turn Brackenport's exclusion of hero and villain economies into a contested civic inheritance. Markets, police and council government continue around a bounded telekinetic ruler.

the-attendance-ledger.note: Six months of anonymous help precede the Northbridge showcase amid modern communications and local disbelief. This story and its direct continuation occupy the proposed later public-power reach before the Bay, rather than being dated by resemblance to Nell’s school world.

the-help-network.note: Three afternoons after the showcase, a contact card starts months of distributed help across countries and oceans. This directly follows Attendance and precedes the Bay in the supplied sequence; the other public institutions are contextual neighbors.

solstice-evening-bell.note: Solstice's coronation and circles lie centuries before the Battle of the Bay; by the battle she is already the last magical girl. The battle precedes the Glass Sea and begins the local aftermath sequence.

the-dress-they-brought-her.note: Damaged post-battle cameras, booking systems and labor procedures misidentify an ordinary prisoner. The supplied sequence places this after the Bay and before the museum; the prisoner is not Solstice.

the-count-was-131072.note: A living witness confronts a digital museum centuries after the Bay. This is the long public-memory aftermath of the same battle, not another immediate recovery scene.

the-future-that-refused-us.note: A hydraulic city has renewed a predictive guarantee every thirty years across three centuries. Ending that local arrangement belongs with mature institutions governing through promised futures, not necessarily the world's final age.

what-i-hate-most.note: Vantress sustains border wards through ceramic work, heat, pressure and municipal crews. It belongs beside engineered public power networks; no common source with the solar branches or an infernal realm is established.

daughter-of-the-sun.note: Four centuries of centralized solar dependence follow the Day of Glass. This established later history comes after Nell's home era and the Bay; decentralizing its branches does not restore or identify another magical system.

the-way-around.note: Paid relic hunters, expedition claims and multiple old scripts meet a dangerous surviving mechanism. Commercial exploration supplies its present-day context; the builders' civilization and the mechanism's category remain unknown.

the-morning-her-hand-moved.note: A community of 5,281 people has kept a thousand years of records on a body treated as permanent ground. Its movement forces evacuation but proves neither divine resurrection nor active magic.

all-accounts-due.note: Centuries of institutional history and thirty-one years of relic travel converge at the Array. Its release is the fixed terminal boundary of old material magic, not the consequence of one nearby city's decline.

four-million-falling.note: Orison’s civic founding story credits human builders after magic’s death. Generations maintain six reactors through incomplete inherited diagrams until fifty minutes force permanent grounding and evacuation. This is a positive remembered relation to extinction, with an unmeasured gap and a local technical fall.

the-five-minute-warranty.note: Coal, steam, quarry work and speaking-wire signals sustain a paid civic workshop. Neglected maintenance becomes a rescue and a permanent repair contract; the story shows functioning industry rather than a lost technology.

the-ordinary-slime.note: Reservoir gauges, chemical assays and collective organism behavior meet a spillway bricked three generations earlier. This maintained agricultural watershed shares a material horizon with road societies; its ordinary biology is not a surviving magical root.
