strength-of-ten: The capital faces a six-day military threat while six depots and lock tolls sustain its army.
A five-day deployment reaches Ninepin under a twenty-day compact.
Before the twentieth day, northern columns begin returning.
the-foundations-remember: Earlier builders create the worked structure beneath the claimed foundation layer
The city’s official founding story claims its first pillars rested on raw stone
A worker's bodily route memory threatens that claim and is preserved inside collateralized personal memory
the-inheritance-remembers: A family preserves a threshold-counting custom after its practical meaning is forgotten
Demolition unseats the iron spike; familiar route cues begin to disappear
Newly painted marks and fresh replies guide the couriers out before the remaining count is consumed
The spike breaks, signs return and the crew secures the route for cleanup in daylight
the-night-harvest: Creatures appear; their bodies enter established markets for roofs, rope, medicine and lamps.
Over three months, preserved throat nodes accumulate as valuable material.
Foreign fighters and local route observations reveal the danger of those stored nodes.
During the convergence, eighty-one preserved nodes are destroyed and ordinary salvage can continue.
the-body-called-one: Four years inside Unit 02 precede extraction into a failing shell
A courier flight continues under bodily and pursuit deadlines
deja-vu-too-late: One consented neural baseline is restored after the triggering loss
The charge is exhausted; material consequences have not rewound
only-eighteen: An elf with almost two centuries of care experience receives six-week-old human twins
Eighteen human years pass with a different weight for their caretaker
the-door-in-the-ivy: Seventeen years after leaving: Clarimond retakes the capital
A conversation beside a childhood door interrupts the public victory
a-little-more-room: An android neighbor arrives and asks about a record
Repeated hallway encounters make room for mutual interest
sakura-hearted: A moon ride carries the couple on a date ten years earlier
Eight years of marriage bring a private anniversary
The rebuilt ride turns on its base beneath paper planets in their apartment
the-second-wearing: The living pendant accompanies Pavia for years and knows only the parts of her life shared with it.
Pavia boxes it for thirty-one years, moving homes while retaining the object.
Her adult niece inherits it in a modern apartment and establishes limits on contact.
The niece shares part of her grief on her own terms; the pendant cannot claim the missing years.
the-one-who-gets-tired: In an undated magical Cusco household, the eldest sibling reaches a human limit
a-throne-neither-wanted: A fatal injury is suspended for roughly a year by royal office
A forecast precedes a freely accepted succession
The original injury takes effect when the support ends
the-vacant-throne: Fifteen years of vacancy approach the end of a caretaker compact
A child arrives with the dead king’s sword and remembered gestures
Recognition does not compel the child to take the throne
a-darkness-written-under-skin: After twenty years believed unmarked: ultraviolet light exposes a hidden birth mark
The graft is withheld pending consultation; a form records the concern without disclosing the ultraviolet finding
friends-of-the-night: Six years of tolerated nearness precede the siege
Three nights of attacks, observation, rescue, and negotiated withdrawal
The host leaves without an established alliance or lasting peace
the-hollow-cask: A public hall is rebuilt around an older cask shell across successive generations
Later operators reduce food and use smoke to coerce the living colony supporting it
A twelve-week harvest reopening aim begins Agnes’s restoration
An early storm exposes the coerced living load
The smaller hall reopens on ordinary posts while the colony receives habitat without compulsory work
the-first-people: Humanity sends roads and empty stations toward stars before younger civilizations arise
Later travelers inherit the routes and turn humanity's priority into a story of legendary elders
A pursued courier reaches a civilian listener in a rain-soaked house on Earth
A rolling root burn destroys the inherited fast-road network; slower rescue craft launch into a still-inhabited sky
the-ten-thousand-year-queen: Roughly ten thousand years after the last pharaoh, adults are reconstructed from fragmentary ancient DNA
Four years after the Vault, linked water and energy works extend Merneith's authority
Across sixty years, the New Egyptian Empire expands over most of the world
The public claims a returned royal house; the reconstructed people possess no original pharaonic memories
the-shadow-that-nested: An unregistered eight-sector sunshade outlasts its original service
Small organisms nest in its housings while ground grids depend on solar charging
A crew opens four shutters enough to reduce eclipse risk while leaving other sectors inhabited
last-watcher-of-jupiter: Thirty years of watch keep a charged Jovian organism below inhabited orbit
An eight-year-old analog repair leaves one frame outside an unclassified command path
Pilots isolate the affected controls and restore containment; the signal's source stays unknown
blade-calls-your-name: An old sky-iron quarry saw survives through a century of repairs in a service blade
A temporary splice remains in place for six years
A returning material fault exposes both the repair history and the guild's record
the-star-that-followed-the-bells: A living ship arrives with damaged route memory and a wounded field vane
Sheep bells become an accidental direction signal over pastoral Ruskala
Three independent satellites answer a repaired turn-taking pattern and support a local ascent
The old stellar route remains lost; the flock returns to ordinary grazing
the-upward-rain: Coastal tradition turns a drowned site into the palace of a legendary kingdom
An exposed seabed reveals repeated hydraulic repairs, communal works and deliberate dismantling
The explorers preserve records and stop short of an untested uphill continuation
The sea returns; the royal story has become a question about a changing working landscape
what-the-town-owed-her: A photograph records Evadne’s flood rescue 114 years earlier
Open promises preserve her youth and keep her inside Mirehaven; descendants inherit expectations, not magical bonds
After another flood rescue, Evadne releases every remaining promise herself
She crosses the town boundary and begins aging again; returning for tea is her choice
lightning-carries-one: Eight years earlier, a same-second crossing leaves Tobin with long, conflicting journey memories
Two later passengers also return altered; Hazel's apparent teleportation has hidden costs
On an ordinary bus route, the siblings examine the notebook and acknowledge what the crossing preserved
the-last-flames: Alexstrasza maintains mortuary procedures older than the kingdoms she can still place, carrying freely left final sensations within herself.
Ygdrane dies and freely leaves flame before the refugees arrive.
Sixty-one living young dragons seek shelter from a northern catastrophe.
Alexstrasza routes the differing patterns through old gates and flues; all sixty-one survive without losing their final flame.
fifty-seven-minutes: At thirty-nine, Orselle receives salt-breath and agelessness from a dying sea creature.
Eighty-six years pass; a harbor book preserves a ritual while losing a crucial instruction.
The misrule rite gives her fifty-seven minutes of divine responsibility for the harbor.
She uses an old relief gate to protect neighboring coves and completes the shore-return, surrendering the gift.
the-future-that-refused-us: Three centuries of successful prediction make spare boats, medicine, timber and trained substitutes seem wasteful.
Six months of hidden preparation teach thousands a counter-cadence for a forty-nine-heartbeat hinge.
The covenant breaks; an untested counterweight jams and the lower ward floods.
The city counts sixty-eight dead and eleven missing, admits the concealed risk, and begins rescue through observation and shared safeguards.
what-i-hate-most: District wards, conduits and mechanical pressure signals place a city’s protection in living hands.
A storm and split conduit expose old masonry failures; a single-controller plan blocks its own spillway.
Ceramic braces take physical loads while two distinct living powers jointly clear the stormglass.
The rulers agree a one-moon service compact with separate vetoes and a safe transfer on withdrawal.
the-way-around: A vast ring structure is built and later receives warnings and marks from earlier visitors.
A professional expedition enters; Ivara’s shots interact with the lattice and leave routes open behind them.
The accumulating paths threaten the explorers until combined observations locate an exterior closure stone.
They return at dawn and record the finding under three names.
the-weight-they-never-counted: Earlier hill populations are fitted for freight; the method is later disputed
Their dense bones and layered tissue persist in a manual road economy
A caravan recognizes and pays for strength that local work had undervalued
rooms-before-sunrise: Five temporarily detached housing bindings are wrongly archived during a floor molt
Living chambers grow outside the official census while their residents remain alive
A pre-sunrise repair keeps the living cultures viable and opens temporary egress; the census and lease entries remain unresolved
the-city-of-eleven-foundations: Eleven different technical districts actively inhabit one basin
A storm exposes failures at their shared boundaries
Crews combine their contemporaneous capacities to repair the ring
thirteen-years-borrowed: Tamaris awakens behind a stranger’s eyes and begins a search through living hosts
Thirteen years pass while her original body ages from thirty-one to forty-four and Nivra builds a life within it
A present-day visit through Calo brings the two living minds together without settling ownership by prior occupancy
the-warmest-person-in-the-room: Brightward already trains and certifies people with varied capacities
The Baroness nickname dates from the previous winter
An orientation morning includes three bounded demonstrations
the-thirteenth-command: Edda accumulates thirty-six years of dispatch experience
An old sensor board and a changed landscape make archived plans unreliable
A roughly eleven-minute command session uses experience while consuming battery cells
anatomy-of-a-god: A practitioner accumulates twelve years of regenerator-care experience
Travel reaches a neglected cult sanctuary
Physical care apparatus complicates the claim that its inhabitant is a god
the-night-she-knew: Private predictive fragments begin in childhood
By sixteen, disclosure still carries fear of disbelief and testing
A Sunday family conversation changes what can be acknowledged

daughter-of-the-sun.note: The Day of Glass is four centuries before the present; the network’s earlier independent period is undated.

the-first-wound.note: The client estimates his age at roughly 25,000 years; this does not date the battle. Other memories are explicitly set 612 and eighty-three years before the present.

the-first-kingdom-was-late-on-taxes.note: Millions of years of displacement; both universal coordinates open

the-small-moon-rose-first.note: 617 shared Ravel days correspond to eleven seconds at Nell’s departure and twelve at Bash’s; their home returns are four months apart. Both material eras precede extinction. Which era comes first in world history is unresolved.

the-count-was-131072.note: The interval from the battle is explicit; the museum’s side of extinction remains open.

the-sky-remembers-us-return.note: Fall → ages of zero → genuinely new magic

tenth-world-lesson.note: Nine years on Eiren's clock, considerably more on Ryo's. The elapsed home interval and destination coordinates are unspecified; the displayed home placement is a reconstruction.

stay-out-of-my-city.note: Nine local years; the earlier-than-Bay location is a proposal, not an established date against other modern stories.

only-eighteen.note: Human and elf lifespans give one interval different weight

the-ten-thousand-year-queen.end: Sixty years of a reconstructed dynasty
the-ten-thousand-year-queen.note: The awakening is roughly ten thousand years after the last pharaoh’s entombment, followed by sixty local years. The ancient genetic sources have their own dates; no original memories are recovered.

thirteen-years-borrowed.start: A living visitor enters repeated host care
thirteen-years-borrowed.end: A return after thirteen local years
thirteen-years-borrowed.note: Thirteen years of living host transfers pass while the original body ages from thirty-one to forty-four. The case's eighty-six hands describe a three-year interval, not the total number of hosts.

a-crown-of-quiet-hours.note: Six weeks to the Charter, seven months to the completed works; Kharost’s dragons are distinct from Varkesh’s collective god.

kite-letters-below.start: The inherited account of surface abandonment
kite-letters-below.note: 812 years is the station's taught interval, not a verified date of surface extinction

the-shadow-that-nested.end: Partial repair beside its new ecology
the-shadow-that-nested.note: The builders and elapsed interval remain unknown; orbital infrastructure has acquired another use

four-million-falling.end: A grounded city and its surviving population
four-million-falling.note: The descent lasts roughly fifty minutes; the city's age and the builders' date remain unresolved

the-room-that-waited.start: An arsenal built by an earlier technical society
the-room-that-waited.end: A warning left by later agrarian finders
the-room-that-waited.note: The generations and cause of knowledge loss are uncounted. The dormant facility does not establish an earlier launch or a nuclear war.

the-first-people.start: Roads built before the younger stellar civilizations
the-first-people.end: The root burn and slow-aid launches
the-first-people.note: An immense undated inheritance ends in one night; enemy occupations and separated populations remain

the-upward-rain.start: An undated sequence of coastal works and abandonment
the-upward-rain.end: One rare day of archaeological access
the-upward-rain.note: Repair phases and dismantling are observable; their dates and the site's complete purpose remain open

lightning-carries-one.end: An ordinary journey eight years later
lightning-carries-one.note: Eight years outside; inconsistent experienced durations and partial aging inside the crossing

where-the-white-elk-went.note: Avarra remembers at least three thousand autumns; the successive land uses are local, not dated Galactic eras.

tea-for-the-first-guest.note: The foundation is about 2,012 years old, with several years of uncertainty; no named empire is placed elsewhere.

the-last-flames.note: The keeper’s mortuary procedures outlast remembered kingdoms; the apparatus’s construction date and the northern threat remain undated.

when-the-eagle-bowed.note: A century separates the execution from the return; no other named dynasty is made a descendant.

the-unfinished-sunset.note: Twenty years outside; repeated experience within one forty-three-minute sunset.

the-peace-they-could-sleep-through.note: A separate twelve-dragon polity; the agreed one-year review is a future condition, not an elapsed century or a completed trial.

fifty-seven-minutes.start: A gift from a dying sea creature
fifty-seven-minutes.note: Eighty-six years of agelessness precede fifty-seven minutes of divine office; these are separate local intervals.

the-night-harvest.start: New creatures in an old trade economy
the-night-harvest.note: Three months of local industry, followed by a six-night investigation; foreign knowledge is older but its place of origin is unspecified.

a-crown-for-the-endless-fire.note: The current mine meets older infrastructure; its builders, fire source and absolute age are unknown.

the-second-wearing.note: The label and family history establish thirty-one boxed years; the pendant could not measure them itself.

the-attendance-ledger.note: Northbridge’s locally low public knowledge of magic is explicit; it is not a date for every contemporary city.

the-help-network.note: Direct Northbridge continuation; expansion takes months. The supplied reading sequence places it before the Bay without a measured gap.

not-about-that.note: Only the reading position before the Bay is supplied; the culture’s founding date and relation to Solstice’s circles remain open.

solstice-evening-bell.note: Centuries separate coronation and battle. The Bay is before the Glass Sea; the circles’ relation to other named teams is unestablished.

the-dress-they-brought-her.note: The supplied sequence is Bay → Dress → Count; the interval to this recovery action is unestablished and the prisoner is not Solstice.

the-future-that-refused-us.note: The covenant renews through nine living readers every thirty years; its local end is not the universal extinction.

what-i-hate-most.note: The storm crisis and one-moon compact are local; the ward system’s founding date is unknown.

the-way-around.note: Three warning scripts and earlier expedition marks precede the visit; their ages and builders remain unassigned.

the-morning-her-hand-moved.start: A thousand years of inhabited ground
the-morning-her-hand-moved.note: The ledgers call the colossus dead, without establishing its origin or true condition; slowing after the impacts does not prove a response.

all-accounts-due.note: The Array was built 302 years before the confrontation; Faris accumulates the relics over thirty-one years. Neither interval is a construction duration. The six ended roots are not universal origins for every earlier magic.

strength-of-ten.note: The deployment is explicitly before extinction; the kingdom’s larger date is unknown.

the-weight-they-never-counted.start: Freight adaptations in earlier hill populations
the-weight-they-never-counted.end: Caravan work in a later manual economy
the-weight-they-never-counted.note: Bodily capacity survives while accounts of whether ancestors were bred, built or repaired diverge; no maker or Galactic coordinate is identified.

the-lights-beyond.start: The wall closes after the horde defeat
the-lights-beyond.end: A commission crosses five hundred years later
the-lights-beyond.note: The enclosed society and its industrial neighbor coexist; their different tools are not sequential world ages.

the-trouble-with-tuesdays.note: The grandfather, Eli and his niece Rose hold the watch in turn. Repeated attempts on one April 22 leave one retained death, followed by many years of Eli’s life. Mae remembers all thirty-one lived deaths only in her continuing afterlife.

the-hollow-cask.start: A hall built around an older cask shell
the-hollow-cask.note: Successive rebuilding, coerced living labor, abandonment and restoration belong to the same institution across undated generations.

what-the-town-owed-her.note: Open promises keep one woman young while the town changes. Their release ends her confinement; the descendants were never magically bound.

gods-afraid-of-grandma.start: A card game interrupted at age sixty-two
gods-afraid-of-grandma.note: Forty-six years of deferred divine obligations unfold among changing roads, worship habits and ordinary medical services. The debts do not make her immortal.

blade-calls-your-name.note: A century of repairs carries the old alloy into a later service blade. A six-year temporary splice fails in the present; the material’s history is longer than the current fault.

the-foundations-remember.start: Worked stone beneath the claimed beginning
the-foundations-remember.end: A worker recovers the forbidden route
the-foundations-remember.note: An already worn and repaired stair, lintel and channel precede an anchor stamped a year before the official First Foundation. The older builders and the full interval remain unknown.

a-throne-neither-wanted.end: A voluntary transfer of the crown
a-throne-neither-wanted.note: The archive records acts without compelling them. A fatal injury from the previous year and its coronation support lead to the present succession; the forecast tradition is older than this crisis.

a-knock-in-someone-elses-sleep.end: A child carries a new reply
a-knock-in-someone-elses-sleep.note: Sixty years after Garnet’s last childhood visits, Cleo carries a reply. The confinement’s full duration and the dream destination’s material coordinates remain unresolved.

connections.label: The light that reaches another sky
connections.note: The established chronology and return story continue Faris and Seyathi’s final fall, then follow ordinary light across ages of perfect zero. Their deaths remain final and no old system returns.

connections.label: One world, a later age
connections.note: The established chronology places Nell and Bash’s old-modern endpoint long before the Glass-Sea era on the same physical world. This orders that endpoint only. Ravel is also a pre-extinction material era, but its order relative to either remains unresolved.

connections.label: The world survives to the Glass Sea
connections.note: The established western-bay chronology places Solstice’s battle before the later Glass-Sea era. No common magical system or measured interval is established.

connections.label: Three afternoons later
connections.note: The Help Network opens at Northbridge on the third afternoon after the showcase, with Cassia, Drita, and Bryn building on the earlier channel compromise.

connections.label: Mutual aid before the Bay
connections.note: The supplied sequence places the Northbridge showcase and its third-afternoon continuation before the Bay. The network shows ordinary communication joining independent magical practices over months; the coronation recalls independent circles, but no organizational descent or measured interval is established.

connections.label: A crowded sky, then the Bay
connections.note: The supplied sequence places Not About That before the Bay. This reconstruction places its everyday public flight in an earlier horizon than the battle’s queen without living subjects. No shared school, cast or institutional descent is established.

connections.label: The aftermath misidentifies a survivor
connections.note: The intended reading sequence places Dress after Solstice and before Count. Its damaged post-battle institutions turn ordinary booking marks into a false survivor claim. The prisoner is not Solstice.

connections.label: From misidentification to misremembrance
connections.note: The subplot’s intended reading sequence places Dress between Solstice and Count, without an established interval. The prisoner and the later museum witness are different people.

connections.label: The witness corrects the count
connections.note: The prose identifies its living museum witness as Solstice Evening Bell, centuries after the same Battle of the Bay. Battle and museum remain in one close local arc; the museum’s pre-extinction side remains editorial.

connections.label: The archmage becomes a teacher
connections.note: Voice establishes Kethra’s qualification; Lock begins with the same named archmage taking a mistreated apprentice and uses her call-link practice. The interval is not dated.

connections.label: Two experiments in government without waking rulers
connections.note: Proposed historical family: two twelve-dragon administrations seek institutions that can outlast continuous personal rule. Kharost retires forty-seven fabricated dead masks and builds watershed sleep works; Varkesh abdicates an actually divine living guise and departs without a veto. The unusually specific parallel supports possible borrowing or rival solutions to a known governance problem. It does not identify the dragons, states or forms of divinity, and their mutual order is open.

connections.label: A home is also a living body
connections.note: Agnes exposes coerced structural labor; Lirenn discovers occupied volume inside living leased rooms. The echo connects a renewed-magical craft society and a much earlier material city without asserting shared biology or building lineage.

connections.label: Who can claim a memory?
connections.note: One-use sensory fragments from retrieved objects and licensed neural extraction make distinct memory problems. The resemblance is thematic, not a shared substance or technological ancestry.

connections.label: The record beneath the monument
connections.note: A museum’s heroic reconstruction and a drowned-king interpretation meet more limited evidence. This is a reader parallel about misremembered history, not a common archive.

connections.label: Humanity becomes an inheritance
connections.note: A dinosaur surface polity and a stellar courier encounter different human legacies. No common departure, station network, or absolute order is established.

connections.label: Learning what the creatures actually do
connections.note: Route observations change how people respond to shadow beasts and throat-node-bearing creatures. The stories establish no common species, invasion, or mechanism.

connections.label: A useful organism changes the question
connections.note: Both communities must reconsider handling practices after observing effects. The slime’s material behavior does not classify the Night Harvest effect or date either settlement.

connections.label: When the ground stops being a promise
connections.note: Evacuation requires precise counts when an inhabited hand moves and when Orison loses lift. The colossus is not assigned a reactor cause; these are not the same fall.

connections.label: The past arrives in a new present
connections.note: An intact displaced village and genetically reconstructed adults confront later institutions. Actual temporal transport and reconstruction remain different processes, not one refounding event.

connections.label: A person falls outside the map
connections.note: A threshold working disrupts a public road; a networked city cannot place an unregistered passenger. The people, technologies, and causes differ, despite the shared recognition problem.

connections.label: The destination keeps its own clock
connections.note: An assignment sequence and the Ravel encounter both resist a flat timeline. Their resemblance proves neither one portal network nor that Ryo’s destinations are Ravel.

connections.label: Crossings bring obligations home
connections.note: Bearer-powered sanctuary crossings and a living market seam both impose local limits. No mechanism, underworld, or ancient route is shared by implication.

connections.label: A return cannot decide for its inhabitants
connections.note: Thirteen Years Borrowed concerns living minds and a volunteer host relay; The Station Between concerns an encountered afterlife. Both make return a problem of whose choice can govern passage. This is a thematic parallel, not a shared mechanism or date.

connections.label: A political offer needs a person’s answer
connections.note: Royal negotiation meets the independent will of the people inside it. This is an ethical parallel between unrelated courts, not a dynasty or a continuation of Ninepin.

connections.label: What the inherited promise costs
connections.note: A solar polity and a witch’s town confront responsibilities accumulated over generations. The juxtaposition does not make promise-binding a descendant of solar fire.

connections.label: A name that can be chosen
connections.note: Different pressures around names and identity invite a joint reading. The stories do not share a name-magic rule, heroic lineage, or cast.

connections.label: One family, unequal capacities
connections.note: An elf caregiver and the mortal eldest of a divine household experience family obligations with unequal capacities. The material town and magical household retain different lifespans, practices and histories.

connections.label: When maintenance becomes forgotten knowledge
connections.note: A proposed long arc places Orison’s working reactor knowledge before agrarian encounters with an unrecognized launch facility. The facility is not identified as Orison, and its builders’ fate and cause of loss remain unknown. Orison’s grounding is a local event, not an established cause of this later condition.

connections.label: The city depends on what lies beneath
connections.note: A hidden older support carries a city that denies its past; eleven different hydraulic foundations must work together during a flood. Both stories make infrastructure consequential. Architectural variety does not establish historical layers, a common origin, or a later change in public knowledge.

connections.label: What a community sees in a body
connections.note: Cody hides shapeshifting while another community treats varied wings as ordinary. The comparison concerns recognition, not a proven change from secrecy to openness: private concealment could exist beside public powers. It does not date these stories or connect their species.

connections.label: Life after the fast roads
connections.note: Proposed historical sequence: the destruction of the inherited interstellar road network is followed by a reach in which stellar travel is fragmented, represented here by the damaged ship over Ruskala and its independent satellite flock. The root burn does not explain the ship's memory damage, and no common route technology is established. The proposed inheritance is a disconnected sky in which local navigation matters again.

connections.label: A profession reaching beyond the city
connections.note: Proposed regional connection: Lanternscrape receives three qualified surveyors with distinct instruments, while the municipal licensing story tests practice against pipe loads and source limits. These are compatible city-and-periphery conditions for circulating technical skills. A shared professional culture is plausible; the same guild, licensing law or exact date is not established.

connections.label: From taught flight to an inhabited sky
connections.note: Proposed long development: Nine Eaves already teaches roof-level flight and survey work using several kinds of focus; the later public sky uses diverse living flight in deliveries, family instruction and agricultural weather. The bridge is the spread of practical aerial knowledge through teaching and work, not a common power source or proof that one academy founded that city.

connections.label: Dragon service beyond hereditary alliance
connections.note: Proposed change in regional political economy: noble-dragon agreements exchange watch, rescue, nesting care and water access, while Qarsis hires a voluntarily migrant ice dragon for bounded municipal work among condensers and trade routes. The comparison supports a later reach where some dragon services travel as paid expertise. It does not claim all alliances ended or that Urumet descends from the earlier partners.

connections.label: Who controls the living heat?
connections.note: Proposed technical connection: Vantress combines living shadow, mineral heat, ceramic braces and ordinary pressure signals; the Glass-Sea branches combine dusk, living solar fire and physical heat-and-water conduits. Methods for sharing loads and limiting a capital’s draw could circulate between such societies. This proposes a field of civic engineering, not identical magic, named teachers or a proven order between the two regions.

connections.label: Enchantment kept in the family
connections.note: Inherited worked wearables enter modern households and small-business economies in both stories. Their proposed shared craft environment is more specific than a resemblance of powers; neither the makers nor the artifacts are connected by established history.

connections.label: The licensed trades reach the threshold
connections.note: This reconstruction carries a history of qualified work from municipal craft assessment to modern doorway certification. It proposes a recurring institutional tradition, not a surviving guild, common city or shared magic.

connections.label: Teaching extraordinary work
connections.note: Field practice, technical instruction and professional expectations connect an old collegium with a later modern college in this reconstruction. Their capacities and institutions remain different; no school descent or inherited flight system is established.

connections.label: Bodies can outlast the industries that shaped them
connections.note: A proposed sequence puts a civilization of routine bodily design before manual road communities carrying ancient freight adaptations. Weight supplies the actual inherited-body evidence; seedglass is not identified as its cause, and no common population or manufacturer is established.

connections.label: Living districts need a common city
connections.note: Living housing, district boundaries and shared civic services place these cities in a compatible technical horizon. This is a proposed institutional context, not proof that the reef tower stands in the eleven-district basin.

connections.label: Government reaches into orbit
connections.note: Water and energy utilities, satellites and orbital control link political authority to a planetary engineering economy. The two states may share a broad technical horizon; no dynasty, succession or common government is established.

connections.label: Fresh replies on older roads
connections.note: Proposed shared historical horizon: courier and municipal route workers encounter older living crossing practices amid courier apps, redevelopment and ordinary traffic. Both passages defeat stored route information and require fresh human replies. These unusually close practical conditions support grouping the stories in one broad pre-extinction horizon. The threshold spike and Briar Host still have different rules; no common maker, town or direct succession is established.

connections.label: Royal power depends on paid public work
connections.note: Proposed neighboring political economies: lock tolls, service wages and repair obligations in one compact closely match the other crown’s negotiated engineers, grain, culverts, toll exemptions and transport. These give the territorial states a concrete shared working context without identifying a dynasty or a common law.

connections.label: Human builders remember magic’s death
connections.note: Orison’s school mosaic credits human builders after magic died. This reconstruction identifies that remembered break with the established extinction while leaving the intervening duration and reliability of the founding image open. The later reactor failure is a separate local technical catastrophe.

connections.label: Civilian work beside the military sky
connections.note: An abandoned military foundry and actively paid tug crews belong to a proposed overlapping orbital economy. Neural systems, repair and embodied lives supply a concrete technical context; neither a common station, manufacturer nor army is established.

historyThreads.title: Gods and authority
historyThreads.description: Local crowns, divine offices and technical states repeatedly gain and lose authority; the extinction alone ends every old material magical capacity.

stages.title: Crowns depend on working roads
stages.note: Royal authority is negotiated through tolls, wages, engineering and neighboring communities that retain the power to act.

stages.title: Divine reigns give way
stages.note: Later gods and long-lived rulers reach the limits of personal government. Distinct dragon administrations surrender claims while human dynasties continue their own successions.

stages.title: The old divine power ends
stages.note: The Ascendancy grows from armistice councils into universal compulsion. All Accounts Due ends old magic, and Orison later celebrates human engineering after magic’s death.

stages.title: Power is built in matter
stages.note: Perfect zero leaves rulers dependent on material institutions. Reconstructed royal identities and continental utilities support a new imperial rise without restored ancient minds.

stages.title: Command loses the fast roads
stages.note: The inherited stellar network is destroyed rather than surrendered to its occupier. In a later proposed reach, new magic begins through living replies that command alone cannot obtain.

stages.title: Gods live among obligations
stages.note: Divine households and water kingdoms recur in the new-magical world with local debts, subjects and limits of their own.

stages.title: Divinity meets practical work
stages.note: A bounded death god participates in civic labor while a practitioner examines an older sanctuary’s claim to godhood. Their different authority remains open to ordinary consequences.

historyThreads.title: Technology and public works
historyThreads.description: Working infrastructure survives some political changes, fails locally in others, and is repeatedly maintained, lost, repurposed or rebuilt.

stages.title: Skills circulate between settlements
stages.note: Colleges, itinerant care and qualified repair connect towns to their working hinterlands; distributed signal polities make another use of trained labor.

stages.title: Cities rework inherited systems
stages.note: The Glass Sea decentralizes a damaged solar inheritance; Vantress develops a different shared service compact. Their technical crews remain part of living cities.

stages.title: Human works rise and fail
stages.note: After extinction, material workshop and maritime societies keep operating. Orison’s irreversible grounding supplies one witnessed technical loss before the proposed later horizon of forgotten arsenals.

stages.title: Ground and orbit are one economy
stages.note: Another technical height joins planetary utilities, living city districts and active civilian orbital work. Unequal access and older structures coexist with advanced engineering.

stages.title: Old structures acquire new uses
stages.note: Road societies salvage an old civic machine while orbital workers maintain a sunshade with a new ecology. The stellar root burn ends a different, much older transport inheritance.

stages.title: New powers enter inhabited services
stages.note: Modern emergency care and public hero work coexist with agricultural and mobile water societies after return; new magic does not require everyone to rebuild the same way.

stages.title: Craft and advanced tools coexist
stages.note: Municipal engines and a restored hall remain useful beside highly mechanized excavation. Later technical cultures retain different capacities rather than occupying one final rung.

historyThreads.title: Bodies and public powers
historyThreads.description: Inhabited bodies carry distinct biological, technical and magical histories; public roles recur without preserving an extinct magical root.

stages.title: Living capacities become livelihoods
stages.note: Healing, bounded military service and privately learned bodily changes inhabit different parts of the older social world.

stages.title: A public sky loses its circles
stages.note: Public powers support education and ordinary aerial work. Centuries after her coronation, Solstice reaches the Bay as the last magical girl and permanently spends her crown.

stages.title: Old capacities reach zero
stages.note: All Accounts Due ends old magical functions while preserving whatever ordinary matter can sustain. The later Long Dark offers no dormant power to lift Orison.

stages.title: Bodies become technical institutions
stages.note: Body plans, living housing and military personas become parts of civic and commercial life. Repair and personal agency continue inside those systems.

stages.title: Bodies outlast their explanations
stages.note: Freight adaptations persist after their makers’ methods become disputed; living surface populations also escape old orbital maps. The eventual first link introduces a genuinely new material capacity.

stages.title: Public powers recur differently
stages.note: Modern cities accommodate varied bodies and professional heroes under new-magical conditions. Local bodily conventions and institutional failures have their own histories.

stages.title: Long lives need present care
stages.note: An approximately twenty-five-thousand-year-old client, a thirteen-year host search and regenerator care put different kinds of long personal history inside current professions. The client’s age does not establish the date of his earliest remembered battle.

historyThreads.title: Memory and landscape
historyThreads.description: The same physical world repeatedly outlasts its accounts of itself: roads, bodies, ruins, records and living witnesses preserve different portions of the past.

stages.title: The older world is already layered
stages.note: An imperial-age tower survives into a bookmender’s commercial world, and paid explorers encounter structures marked by earlier visitors. Nell’s brief departure opens onto another unresolved material era.

stages.title: Land and witnesses outlast regimes
stages.note: Royal land becomes woodland, a living witness corrects centuries of Bay commemoration, and recovered records change how the Glass Sea governs its surviving branches.

stages.title: A break becomes civic memory
stages.note: Orison turns magic’s death into a founding image while copying gaps in engineering diagrams. Later agrarian finders can recognize an exit without recognizing the arsenal around it.

stages.title: Antiquity becomes a political resource
stages.note: Reconstructed rulers build a new empire from ancient identities while another city conceals the older structure supporting its claimed beginning.

stages.title: The inherited accounts are corrected
stages.note: Living ground communities overturn orbital abandonment stories. Humanity’s stellar priority acquires material evidence; much later, ordinary light shows the old extinction without reviving its dead.

stages.title: The new world makes its own past
stages.note: Photographs and divine debts preserve changing local obligations. A later proposed Crucible catastrophe leaves survivors and damaged countryside instead of ending the world.

stages.title: The past disputes its monuments
stages.note: Coastal repairs complicate a drowned-king tradition, a displaced village confronts its own founding legend, and an old memory retains limits that present expertise cannot erase.
